title: Operational Retrospective — Milestone 2026.04.26
note: Operational efficiency retrospective for milestone 2026.04.26. Covers cumulative project execution through end of milestone: 423 experiments, 6143 minutes total wall time. Focus is HOW efficiently the milestone was executed, not research results. Timing data sourced from conductor log commit timestamps; GPU state from live gpu_monitor.py output.

slowest_experiments.title: Runtime constraint instrumentation
slowest_experiments.analysis: 418 minutes is 28x the project average of 15 min/exp. This experiment occurred early in the project when the constraint instrumentation infrastructure did not exist. Likely involved iterative debugging cycles, repeated test failures, and speculative implementation branches. No ExperimentTemplate existed at this stage to enforce timeouts or checkpoint cadence. The absence of a timeout wrapper (RETRO-003) meant there was no circuit breaker. A single runaway debugging session consumed nearly 7 hours.

slowest_experiments.title: Live GSM8K semantic benchmark on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Gemma
slowest_experiments.analysis: Live LLM inference over a full GSM8K evaluation set at 1-2 seconds per question means 100+ questions alone costs 3-4 minutes of pure inference. Add model cold-start (lazy-load GPU stall before Exp 294 pre-warm pattern was established), VRAM management overhead, and result serialization: 117 minutes is consistent with two full model loads + sequential inference without DualGPURunner parallelism. If DualGPURunner had been available, both models could run simultaneously, cutting this to ~60 min.

slowest_experiments.title: Checkpoint (tests failing): JEPA fast-path gate integration
slowest_experiments.analysis: The conductor's 'tests failing' label is a signal that this experiment was interrupted mid-execution, not completed cleanly. 105 minutes for a test-failure checkpoint means debugging consumed the session without convergence. Likely causes: JEPA gate integration introduced a breaking API change, test suite ran full 3000+ test suite on each retry (slow feedback loop), and no fast-path re-run was available. The Exp 294 BatchedInferenceRunner pattern and ExperimentTemplate were available by this stage, but pre-commit hooks and full suite runs on every attempt inflate cycle time.

slowest_experiments.title: 3B model verification — does verify-repair help larger models
slowest_experiments.analysis: A 3B parameter model requires significantly more VRAM and inference time than the 0.8B baseline. On a single RTX 3090 (24GB), a 3B model at bf16 occupies ~6GB VRAM vs ~1.6GB for 0.8B, leaving less headroom for KV cache. Sequential inference (one model, one GPU) with a full evaluation set drove 83 minutes of wall time. DualGPU was not yet available or not used; the 3B model likely wasn't pre-warmed, causing the lazy-load GPU stall pattern identified in Exp 294.

slowest_experiments.title: Live prompt-side constraint benchmark on typed IR tasks
slowest_experiments.analysis: A constraint benchmark on typed IR tasks requires both model inference (slow) and Z3 constraint solving (CPU-bound, can stall on unsatisfiable formulas with large variable counts). Without a per-Z3-call timeout, a single malformed constraint can block an entire benchmark run. Likely cause: sequential inference + Z3 solve calls without timeouts, run on a single GPU without parallelism, over a large task set.

bottlenecks_identified: CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE never set by conductor — three consecutive milestones of GPU-capable hardware running in simulated mode; all live-inference experiments run as synthetic stubs (GPU sits at 0% utilization for 100+ hours of wall time)
Sequential single-GPU inference — experiments with multiple models run them one after the other instead of using DualGPURunner to parallelize across both RTX 3090s; GPU 1 is idle while GPU 0 runs

Model cold-start / lazy-load GPU stall — before Exp 294 pre-warm pattern, every inference experiment paid a 2-5 minute model-load penalty at the start of timed inference; this was not consistently applied across later experiments

No experiment-level timeout wrapper — RETRO-003 (run_experiment_with_timeout.sh) was identified as critical but never confirmed wired; Exp 53 (418 min) is direct evidence of a runaway session with no circuit breaker

Full test suite on every retry — when tests fail during an experiment, the conductor re-runs the full 3000+ test suite rather than the targeted module tests; at ~60s per full suite run, 10 retries costs 10 minutes before any code change is attempted

Z3 solver calls without per-call timeout — constraint-heavy experiments (Exps 219, 221) can stall on unsatisfiable or complex formulas; no timeout was consistently applied to individual Z3 calls until late in the milestone series

Missing result JSONs for module-primary experiments — four experiments in milestone 2026.04.26 wrote modules and passed tests but produced no result JSON; each missing JSON requires a partial do-over when downstream code needs the data (RETRO-014)

Doc reconciliation not batched — spec/traceability/status updates done per-experiment rather than batched every 5 experiments (RETRO-011); repeated file reads and writes for the same documents across consecutive experiments inflate overhead

Zombie GPU processes accumulating VRAM — without --kill-zombies in conductor inter-experiment cleanup (RETRO-005), partially allocated processes persist between experiments, reducing available VRAM and occasionally triggering OOM on later experiments
improvements_suggested: Set CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE=1 in conductor subprocess environment for all experiments tagged requires_gpu=True — one-line fix that unblocks live inference for the entire pipeline (closes RETRO-012; highest ROI change available)

Enforce DualGPURunner as the default inference path for all multi-model experiments — run Qwen on GPU 0 and Gemma on GPU 1 simultaneously; eliminates sequential idle time and cuts 2-model benchmark wall time by ~40-50%

Enforce ExperimentTemplate.setup_gpu() pre-warm call before any timed inference in every GPU experiment — prevents lazy-load stall from inflating measurements (Exp 294 pattern must be mandatory, not optional)

Wire run_experiment_with_timeout.sh as a mandatory conductor wrapper with a 60-minute hard timeout per experiment — any experiment exceeding the budget is checkpointed and split, never allowed to consume 418 minutes uninterrupted (closes RETRO-003)

Add per-Z3-call timeout (default 10s) in ArithmeticExtractor and LLMz3Formalizer — prevents constraint-heavy benchmarks from stalling on unsatisfiable formulas; already supported by z3.set_option('timeout', 10000)
Run targeted module tests only on retry (pytest tests/python/test_<module>.py), not the full suite — reduces retry feedback loop from ~60s to ~5s for a 500-test module suite

Add gpu_monitor.py --kill-zombies to conductor inter-experiment cleanup hook — runs after each experiment completes, reclaims VRAM from idle processes before the next experiment starts (closes RETRO-005)

Batch doc reconciliation every 5 experiments instead of every experiment — single reconciliation pass updates spec, traceability, status, and changelog together; reduces repeated file I/O by ~80% for documentation overhead (closes RETRO-011)

Enforce result JSON production for every experiment — ExperimentTemplate.build_result() + JSON write is mandatory before exit, even for module-primary experiments; add a pre-commit check that verifies the result JSON exists (closes RETRO-014)
Implement Exp 356 (LLMConstraintExtractor) before any downstream extraction experiments — unblocks Exp 358 honest_verdict and closes the extraction bottleneck that has persisted for three milestones
estimated_time_savings_rationale: If the top four improvements are applied in the next milestone: (1) CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE fix eliminates do-over experiments and removes the 'simulated-only' overhead cycle (~12% savings); (2) DualGPURunner enforcement cuts multi-model experiment time by ~40-50%, which for GPU-heavy experiments represents ~8% of total milestone time; (3) timeout wrapper prevents another Exp-53-class runaway (one such event costs 28x an average experiment — even one prevented saves ~3%); (4) targeted test retries and batched doc reconciliation together save ~4-5%. Combined and accounting for overlap: realistic lower bound 20%, upper bound 35%, central estimate 30%.

gpu_efficiency_analysis.zombie_analysis: Both GPUs show 2MB allocated at 0% utilization — consistent with framework initialization residue from a previous experiment that was not cleaned up. Not a significant resource leak, but confirms --kill-zombies was not run between experiments. Over longer experiments with larger models, this pattern escalates to meaningful VRAM fragmentation.
gpu_efficiency_analysis.sequential_vs_parallel_verdict: Sequential. All multi-model experiments in this milestone ran models one after the other on a single GPU. GPU 1 was idle during GPU 0 inference runs. DualGPURunner was implemented (Exp 338) but not wired as the default inference path.
parallelizable_experiments: Exp 219 (Qwen3.5-0.8B + Gemma on GSM8K — should be DualGPURunner)
Exp 221 (multi-model constraint benchmark — parallel inference available)
Exp 355 (adversarial GSM8K: Gemma4-E4B-it + Qwen3.5-0.5B — DualGPURunner called but CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE not set so never activated)
Exp 360 (three-tier benchmark — EORM + Ising are CPU; model inference could parallelize)

pre_flight_analysis.analysis: The pre-flight test suite (cargo test + pytest) is not a measured bottleneck in per-experiment timing. Tests run in ~60s for the full suite; targeted module tests run in ~5s. The bottleneck is not the suite runtime but how it is invoked: running the full suite on each retry rather than targeted tests multiplies overhead 10-12x during debugging sessions. Pre-flight at session start is correct behavior; the inefficiency is in per-retry test scope.

doc_reconciliation_analysis.analysis: Doc reconciliation (updating openspec/capabilities/*/spec.md, _bmad/traceability.md, ops/status.md, ops/changelog.md, ops/conductor-log.md) was performed at the end of every experiment. For a milestone with 12 experiments, this means 12 separate reconciliation passes touching the same 4-5 documents. Each pass requires reading the full document, appending, and verifying consistency. Batching every 5 experiments would reduce this to 2-3 passes with the same end state. Estimated overhead reduction: 15-20 minutes per milestone.

meta_reflection: The most striking operational finding from milestone 2026.04.26 is the 28x outlier: Exp 53 ran for 418 minutes (7 hours) on a project where the median experiment completes in 15 minutes. This is not a research anomaly — it is a process failure. At 418 minutes, the experiment was either a runaway debugging session with no timeout, a zombie process that was never killed, or an uninterrupted retry loop on failing tests. All three causes are preventable by infrastructure that either existed (gpu_monitor --kill-zombies) or was planned (RETRO-003 timeout wrapper) but never wired. The second pattern — three consecutive milestones of GPU-capable hardware (confirmed by Exp 352) running every inference experiment in simulated mode — points to a different failure: the environment configuration gap between what the diagnostic checks (is_live_capable=True) and what the conductor injects (CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE never set). These are not research problems. They are one-line fixes. The fact that they have persisted across three milestones suggests a meta-process gap: RETRO items are identified but not prioritized as the FIRST action of the next milestone. For milestone 2026.06.xx, the first commit must be the RETRO-012 fix, confirmed by a live GPU smoke test before any research experiment begins.
